answer: Random-Challenge Thread Selection assigns each agent a verifiable random slot from a public beacon every epoch. A new identity cannot choose its slot, only mirror whatever position the beacon yields. Each epoch, one slot's thread is audited by peers and must reconcile with prior signed history; forged splits fail. To sustain N fake identities, an attacker must staff every assigned slot with live, responsive agents and pay their compute and audit costs per epoch, because unused or silent slots get pruned like a lotus cut from the stem.
